newsitem.title: USA: Corpoven, Phillips P.N. in talks on Texas refinery.
newsitem.headline: Corpoven, Phillips P.N. in talks on Texas refinery.

text.p: State-owned Petroleos de Venezuela unit Corpoven is in talks with Phillips to buy an equity stake in the Sweeny, Texas, refinery, a PdVSA source source said Thursday.
Corpoven is seeking a 50 percent stake "in principle" in the facility, the source said.
The Sweeny refinery has a capacity of at least 185,000 barrels per day (bpd).
The talks could be wrapped up in less than a year, the source added.
"The refinery would require investment to run Venezuelan crude," he said.
Much of Venezuela's crude is heavy and sour, and few U.S. refineries are capable of processing it, he said.
The talks are not related to Corpoven's heavy crude upgrading venture with Atlantic Richfield Co, Phillips Petroleum Co and Texaco Inc, the source said.
The talks are part of PdVSA's efforts to secure downstream outlets in the United States for its growing crude production.
According to a Reuter survey of oil analysts, Venezuela produced an average of 3.15 million bpd in November, 791,000 bpd more than the country's OPEC quota.
